374732.title: The lifting conjecture for Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs
374732.statement:
Let $C_{n_1}(R_1)$ and $C_{n_2}(R_2)$ be circulant graphs satisfying

$$
C_{n_1}(R_1)\Box C_{n_2}(R_2)=C_{n_1n_2}(R)\cong C_{n_1n_2}(n_2R_1\cup n_1R_2)
$$

for some $R$ and $gcd(n_1,n_2)=1$. Suppose that, for some $m_1$, $t_1$, and $S_1$,

$$
C_{n_1}(R_1)\cong_{T2_{n_1,m_1,t_1}}C_{n_1}(S_1).
$$

**Lifting conjecture.** Then, for some $S$,

$$
C_{n_1n_2}(R)\cong_{T2_{n_1n_2,m_1,t_1n_2}}C_{n_1n_2}(S).
$$

The conjecture asserts that a Type-2 isomorphism on one relatively prime factor lifts to the corresponding product circulant graph; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.

374782.title: Cox–McGinnis–Marchant conjecture on finiteness of accumulation points
374782.statement: Let ${\mathcal H}$ be a non-trivial hereditary property of graphs, and call $p\in[0,1]$ an accumulation point when the edit-distance function of ${\mathcal H}$ is not locally determined by finitely many CRGs. **Cox–McGinnis–Marchant's conjecture.** Any non-trivial hereditary property has only finitely many accumulation points. Accumulation points can occur for hereditary properties, including at interior values such as $1/4$, while the supplied source gives no resolution of this general finiteness assertion.

374870.title: Critical-excess conjecture for distinguishable tree assignments
374870.statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-weakly-partition-connected hypergraph on $t$ vertices. A tree assignment of $H$ assigns a tree to every hyperedge occurrence, and the resulting labelled graph has a **$k$-distinguishable** tree assignment when its $k$-tree decomposition is uniquely determined by its signature.

**Critical-excess conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{e\in E(H)}(|e|-1)=k(t-1),
$$

then $H$ has a $k$-distinguishable tree assignment.

This is presented as the natural repair of the refuted literal conjecture, after adding the missing critical-excess equality. The supplied text does not establish whether this repaired statement is proved or remains open.
374870.finding: Latest v4 Conjecture1.5, definitions, Theorem2.6 and proof, Remark3.5 read. Criticality gives a full tree decomposition for every assignment, not a singleton signature fiber. Two path labels on three vertices have two decompositions sharing the split signature, yet also have unique extreme signatures.
374870.precise_gaps_and_limits: Need one assignment with one singleton fiber for every critical WPC hypergraph. Failure of one fiber or one assignment is not the negation of this existential claim.

374967.title: Duality conjecture for transmuted preorder M-triangles
374967.statement:
Let $\tau$ be a preorder of size $n$, let $P_\tau$ be its lattice-point poset, and let $\overline M_{P_\tau}$ be the transmuted $M$-triangle. **Transmuted M-triangle duality conjecture.**

$$
(xy)^n\overline M_{P_\tau}(1/x,1/y)=\overline M_{P_\tau}(y,x).
$$

Equivalently, if $L_\tau$ is a lattice realization as in the preceding conjecture, then $M_{L_\tau}(x,y)=M_{L_\tau^\ast}(x,y)$, where $L_\tau^\ast$ is the dual lattice. The source provides no resolution.

375025.title: Ballantine–Beck–Merca injectivity conjecture for elementary symmetric partitions
375025.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. A **partition** of $n$ is a weakly decreasing sequence of positive integers with size $n$ and length $\ell$. For $1\leq j\leq\ell$, define $\operatorname{pre}_j(\lambda)$ to be the partition whose parts are the products of all $j$-element subcollections of the parts of $\lambda$. **Ballantine–Beck–Merca's injectivity conjecture.** For $j\geq 2$, the function $\operatorname{pre}_j$ is injective on the set of partitions of size $n$ and length $\ell\geq j$. This conjecture is false: the $j=2$ case is solved, while the case $\ell=j$ has been disproved, and the present paper disproves the claim for $\ell=2j$ when $j\geq3$.

375028.title: The upper-ledge containment conjecture
375028.statement:
Let $\Pi$ be the set of pairs of partitions, let $i\in\mathbb{Z}_2$, and let $\mathcal{X}_i:\Pi\rightarrow\mathcal{UL}$ be the associated map to upper ledge diagrams. If $\pi,\tilde{\pi}\in\Pi$ and $\tilde{\pi}$ is obtained by deleting the last row of one component of $\pi$, then **upper-ledge containment conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{X}_i(\tilde{\pi})\subseteq\mathcal{X}_i(\pi).
$$

The paper states this as a consequence that would follow from the preceding partition-containment conjecture, linking multipartition operations to upper-ledge crystal combinatorics.

375083.title: Davoodi–Javadi–Kamranian–Raeisi multicolor star-forest conjecture
375083.statement:
Let $t$ be an integer, let $a_{1},a_{2},\dots,a_{t}$ be positive integers, and set

$$
a=\sum_{s=1}^{t}a_{s}.
$$

For each $s\in[t]$, let $n_{1}^{s}\geq n_{2}^{s}\geq\cdots\geq n_{a_{s}}^{s}\geq1$ be integers. For each $k\in[a]\backslash[t-1]$, define

$$
\ell_{k}=\max\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{t}n_{i_{s}}^{s}-t+1:\sum_{s=1}^{t}i_{s}=k\right\}.
$$

**Davoodi–Javadi–Kamranian–Raeisi conjecture.** The multicolor size Ramsey number satisfies

$$
\hat{r}\left(\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{a_{1}}K_{1,n_{i}^{1}},\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{a_{2}}K_{1,n_{i}^{2}},\dots,\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{a_{t}}K_{1,n_{i}^{t}}\right)=\sum_{k=t}^{a}\ell_{k}.
$$

This extends the two-color star-forest conjecture to multiple colors and is presented as a conjectural generalization; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
375083.finding: Source introduction, two-color Conjecture1.1 and Theorems1.2/1.3 read. Uniform two-color star-forest results do not resolve arbitrary sequences in arbitrarily many colors.
375083.precise_gaps_and_limits: Need multicolor lower bound and matching upper construction for all sequences. No claimed counterexample based on degenerate t or an infeasible index tuple.
375083.actual_review_depth: Source introduction, two-color Conjecture1.1 and Theorems1.2/1.3 read. Uniform two-color star-forest results do not resolve arbitrary sequences in arbitrarily many colors.

375296.title: The four-pattern involution equidistribution conjecture for length-2 mesh patterns
375296.statement:
Let $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ be the four length-$2$ mesh patterns displayed in the source, with mesh-cell sets respectively $\{(1,2),(1,1),(2,1),(0,0)\}$, $\{(2,2),(0,1),(1,1),(1,0)\}$, $\{(0,2),(1,1),(2,1),(1,0)\}$, and $\{(1,2),(0,1),(1,1),(2,0)\}$, and with points at $(1,1)$ and $(2,2)$. An **involution** is a permutation whose cycles have length at most $2$.

**Four-pattern involution equidistribution conjecture.** The patterns

$$
\{p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4\}
$$

are equidistributed on involutions.

The source notes that the first two patterns and the last two patterns are trivially equidistributed via reverse and complement. The conjectural content is the asserted equidistribution of the displayed collection on involutions.

Let $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ be the four length-$2$ mesh patterns displayed in the source, with mesh-cell sets respectively $\{(1,2),(1,1),(2,1),(0,0)\}$, $\{(2,2),(0,1),(1,1),(1,0)\}$, $\{(0,2),(1,1),(2,1),(1,0)\}$, and $\{(1,2),(0,1),(1,1),(2,0)\}$, and with points at $(1,1)$ and $(2,2)$. An **involution** is a permutation whose cycles have length at most $2$.

**Four-pattern involution equidistribution conjecture.** The patterns

$$
\{p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4\}
$$

are equidistributed on involutions.

The source notes that the first two patterns and the last two patterns are trivially equidistributed via reverse and complement. The conjectural content is the asserted equidistribution of the displayed collection on involutions.

375373.title: The even-by-even hook Conway-pair conjecture
375373.statement: A partition is a Young diagram, and its **Conway pair** is the pair of game-theoretic invariants used in the Conway–Gurvich–Ho classification. An **even-by-even hook** is a hook with an even number of rows and an even number of columns. **Even-by-even hook conjecture.** A partition $\lambda$ has Conway pair $(0,1)$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an even-by-even hook. Conway pairs $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$ play an important role in the classification scheme; the source leaves this characterization as a conjecture.
375373.finding: Conway pair definition, terminal convention, Theorems17 and19 with full proofs, Conjecture6 read. Even-by-even hooks have CP(0,1) by explicit mex induction. Converse for all nonempty nonhooks remains unproved.

375422.title: Caoduro–Khodamoradi–Paat–Shepherd simplex exchange conjecture
375422.statement: Let $S$ and $T$ be $d$-dimensional simplices whose interiors contain the origin. A **vertex exchange** replaces one vertex while producing another $d$-dimensional simplex whose interior contains the origin. **Caoduro–Khodamoradi–Paat–Shepherd's simplex exchange conjecture.** Any two such simplices can be transformed into each other via at most $d+1$ vertex exchanges, while always maintaining the origin in the interior. The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is disproved.

375496.title: Kalai's monomial-ideal diameter conjecture
375496.statement: Let $I\subset k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a square-free monomial ideal generated in degree $d$ and having a linear presentation. Let $G_I$ be the graph whose vertices are the minimal monomial generators of $I$, labeled by the indices of their factors. **Kalai's monomial-ideal diameter conjecture.** The diameter of $G_I$ is bounded above by a polynomial in $d$. This is the algebraic restatement of Kalai's Abstract Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture, connecting graph diameter bounds with linear presentations of square-free monomial ideals; the source does not specify whether the conjecture has been resolved.
375496.finding: Source AppendixA definitions and ConjectureA.3 read. Non-Hirsch examples diam>d concern a linear candidate bound, not existence of an arbitrary polynomial bound in d.
375496.precise_gaps_and_limits: A fixed finite graph cannot refute an unspecified polynomial bound; need a superpolynomial family with linear-presentation certificates, or a uniform bound proof.
375496.actual_review_depth: Source AppendixA definitions and ConjectureA.3 read. Non-Hirsch examples diam>d concern a linear candidate bound, not existence of an arbitrary polynomial bound in d.

375578.title: Matsubara-Heo–Telen dual-degree conjecture for reciprocal linear spaces
375578.statement:
Let $L\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n$ be a linear subspace of dimension $d$ not contained in any coordinate hyperplane, let $L^{-1}$ be its reciprocal linear space, and let $M=\operatorname{M}(L)$ be the matroid represented by $L$. Write $\beta(M)$ for the beta invariant of $M$, and denote the projective dual of $L^{-1}$ by $(L^{-1})^\vee$. **Matsubara-Heo–Telen's dual-degree conjecture.** If the matroid $M$ is connected, then $(L^{-1})^\vee$ is a hypersurface of degree

$$
2^d\beta(M).
$$

This conjecture predicts the degree of the dual hypersurface in the connected case, complementing the associated dual-defectivity claim; the source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

375625.title: Dombi's obstruction conjecture for strict monotonicity of higher-fold representation functions
375625.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ and let $h\geq 1$ be an integer. Define the ordered $h$-fold representation function by

$$
R_{A,h}(n)=\#\{(a_1,\ldots,a_h)\in A^h:a_1+\cdots+a_h=n\}.
$$

The complement $\mathbb N\setminus A$ is **co-infinite** when it is infinite. **Dombi's conjecture.** If $\mathbb N\setminus A$ is infinite, then $R_{A,h}(n)$ cannot be eventually strictly increasing. This conjecture proposes an obstruction to strict monotonicity for representation functions of sets with infinite complement; the provided text gives no resolution, while Dombi's earlier result shows that eventual non-strict increase can occur for suitable co-infinite sets when $h>4$.
375625.finding: Source Dombi conjecture, Shallit TheoremC and Theorem1.1 read. Base4-leading1-or2 set B has infinite complement and strictly increasing ordered three-fold representation function.
375625.precise_gaps_and_limits: Complete public theorem bridge: choose h=3, observe all3*4^m are omitted, apply positive first differences. No new proof claim; source proof of Theorem1.1 not fully read.
375625.actual_review_depth: Source Dombi conjecture, Shallit TheoremC and Theorem1.1 read. Base4-leading1-or2 set B has infinite complement and strictly increasing ordered three-fold representation function.

375626.title: Signature-native graph recovery for sparse multivariate Hawkes kernels
375626.statement:
For a sparse multivariate Hawkes process, let $A_T^{ij}$ denote the cross-area between coordinates $i$ and $j$ over a time horizon $T$, and let the associated excitation graph encode the directed excitation relationships between coordinates. **Signature-native graph recovery.** For sparse multivariate Hawkes kernels, the sign pattern of the expected cross-areas

$$
\{\mathbb{E}[A_T^{ij}]\}_{i<j}
$$

over one or several horizons recovers the dominant directed excitation graph after controlling for common baselines and self-excitation. This would provide a signature-based method for recovering directional interaction structure from Hawkes-process data; the statement is presented as an open conjecture, and its precise identifiability conditions remain to be established.
375626.finding: Section10 exact antisymmetric-area definition, Proposition10.1 and full proof, Theorem10.2 and full proof, Conjecture15.1 read. Symmetric reciprocal cross-excitation and equal independent baselines yield identical all-zero expected antisymmetric areas.
375626.precise_gaps_and_limits: This obstructs full-support recovery, but dominant graph, sparsity threshold, permitted controls and tie conventions are unspecified. Does not refute an asymmetric-dominance endpoint; no candidate or Pi plan.

375673.title: Tang–Liu–Wang positive p-energy conjecture
375673.statement:
For a graph $G$, define its positive adjacency $p$-energy by

$$
\mathcal E_p^+(G)=\sum_{\lambda_i(G)>0}\lambda_i(G)^p.
$$

Let $p\ge2$ be a real number, and let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices. **Tang–Liu–Wang's positive $p$-energy conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal E_p^+(G)\ge \mathcal E_p^+(P_n).
$$

The conjecture asserts that among connected graphs on $n$ vertices, the path $P_n$ minimizes positive adjacency $p$-energy. Positive and negative $p$-energies arise in spectral graph theory and have applications to chromatic and related graph parameters; the source does not report a resolution of this conjecture.
375673.finding: Companion Conjecture3.1, Theorems3.2/3.3 context and branch discussion read; main focused companion retrieved, not fully reviewed. Bipartite/all odd-integer cases do not give all connected graphs and real p>=2.
375673.precise_gaps_and_limits: Need remaining nonbipartite real-p inequality, especially p=2; real power comparison cannot be inferred from discrete odd moments alone.
375673.actual_review_depth: Companion Conjecture3.1, Theorems3.2/3.3 context and branch discussion read; main focused companion retrieved, not fully reviewed. Bipartite/all odd-integer cases do not give all connected graphs and real p>=2.

375770.title: The stable Grothendieck Lam–Postnikov–Pylyavskyy inequality
375770.statement:
Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions, and let $\widetilde G_\lambda(\mathbf x)$ denote the stable Grothendieck polynomial. Write $\lambda\vee\mu$ and $\lambda\wedge\mu$ for the join and meet of the two partitions, and interpret $\leq_{\widetilde G}$ as the stable Grothendieck positivity order. **Stable Grothendieck LPP inequality.**

$$
\widetilde G_\lambda(\mathbf x)\widetilde G_\mu(\mathbf x) \leq_{\widetilde G} \widetilde G_{\lambda\vee\mu}(\mathbf x)\widetilde G_{\lambda\wedge\mu}(\mathbf x).
$$

This is the Grassmannian specialization of the vexillary Grothendieck inequality and was previously predicted by Thomas and Yong. It remains open.
375770.finding: Source Conjecture1.17 and surrounding specialization discussion read. Schur positivity and monomial positivity are weaker than positivity in the stable Grothendieck basis.
375770.precise_gaps_and_limits: Need actual stable-Grothendieck-positive expansion for all partition pairs or exact negative coefficient witness with full basis semantics. No basis-change shortcut.
375770.actual_review_depth: Source Conjecture1.17 and surrounding specialization discussion read. Schur positivity and monomial positivity are weaker than positivity in the stable Grothendieck basis.
